# whatIf only simulates for the literal string 'true'

**Claim.** Only the exact value `true` simulates. Every other non-empty value — including `1` and `yes` — is read as false and performs the merge for real, and the response is identical either way, so nothing in it reveals which one happened.

Applies to: `~1people~1{vanId}~1mergeInto/put`

## Observed exchange

_Two records to merge: the primary survives, the secondary is consumed._

```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Rosa",
  "lastName": "Delgado-{scope}",
  "emails": [
    {
      "email": "rosa.delgado-{scope}@example.com"
    }
  ]
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```
```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Rosa",
  "lastName": "Delgado-{scope}",
  "emails": [
    {
      "email": "rdelgado-{scope}@example.com"
    }
  ]
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000002
{
  "vanId": 100000002,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```

_Ask for a simulation with whatIf=yes — truthy in every language a caller might write this in. The 200 below is exactly what a real simulation returns._

```http
PUT /people/100000002/mergeInto?whatIf=yes

{
  "vanId": 100000001
}

→ 200
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001
}
```

_But nothing was simulated. The secondary is gone for good — only the literal string `true` suppresses the write._

```http
GET /people/100000002

→ 404
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "NOT_FOUND",
      "text": "The specified resource cannot be found."
    }
  ]
}
```
